meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son's zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.

"The zero stands." On what basis, Hale, and who decided it before anyone spoke to Owen? Your own procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and I'm writing down that nobody called me.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

Okay. I'm writing down October 15, and I want to see the line you say isn't in Hamlet. An outline that argues one thing and an essay that argues another is a student changing his mind, so what else do you have?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that I receive an apology for how it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
Cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal involved if she doesn't get them.
What moved her: "Let me show you what I actually have", because a dated outline and a specific line gave her something to write down, though she hasn't seen either yet.
What cost ground: "I don't have time for this. The zero stands.", because it defended the zero before any process was owned and left her with only the procedure to argue from.
Try next time: in your first line, own that the zero went in before the call home, then put the Hamlet line and the October 15 outline in front of her at once so she can check them herself.
